text:
RECOMMENDATION: DON'T RAISE IT
LIKELIHOOD: 15

The panel's composition tells you almost nothing. Four women on a panel is statistically unremarkable in many ministries, and panel sex doesn't reliably predict the sex of the candidate chosen. Raising it as your opening move signals grievance rather than substance, and it tends to make an employer defensive and less forthcoming — exactly the opposite of what you need.

Your real issue is procedural: you asked for written reasons two weeks ago and got silence. Chase that in writing, with a deadline, citing whatever access-to-information or recruitment-transparency rules apply. Ask specifically how candidates were scored against the published criteria.

If those documents show criteria shifted or your qualifications were scored oddly, you'll have something concrete. Composition alone isn't it.
